thread:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Canary slice 'thin-slice-eu-west-1' showing latency & throughput regression post-deploy. Canary traffic at 40%. Detected 09:12 UTC. Auto-page on-call.
priya: I'm on it — paging runtime and release. Can someone share the rollout ID and what changed in this slice?
deploy-bot: rollout_id=rl-2026-11-09-87c, release=service-runtime@v3.14.0, feature_flags=[release.batch_prefetch_v2:true], canary=40%, regions=[eu-west-1 thin-slice].
ben: saw the alert in dashboards — p50 jumped from ~60ms to 300-600ms, p95 spiking to 2.4s for a subset of hosts. Throughput per host dropped ~35%.
alex: getting logs now. There's repeated kernel fallback lines on several pods: ``kernel_selector: fallback to kernel-compat-avx due to kernel_launch_timeout``. Also see batching queue growth and KV cache misses.
mike: likely the new kernel scheduling path in v3.14 had a regression under thin-slice memory constraints. Batching config `batch_size_hint` seems higher and combined with prefetch change is increasing mem pressure -> kernel launch fallback.
emma: customer telemetry shows 0.8% of requests from acme-payments have 3-5x latency for critical endpoints. Not yet widespread but it's a paying customer on dedicated route. We should treat as P1 until we have targeted rollback.
priya: agreed P1. Immediate mitigation options: 1) flip feature flag `release.batch_prefetch_v2` off via flag service, 2) throttle canary to 0% (kill-switch), 3) emergency rollback to v3.13. Prioritize fastest with least blast radius.
alex: I can flip the flag, but we need to coordinate with release to avoid state mismatch.
ben: flag toggle is fastest. Use internal `flagon` API: ``POST https://flagon.internal/api/flags/release.batch_prefetch_v2/toggle {"state":"off","actor":"priya"}``
priya: doing it now. ``curl -s -X POST 'https://flagon.internal/api/flags/release.batch_prefetch_v2/toggle' -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx' -d '{"state":"off"}'``
ops-bot: action log: flag toggled by priya at 09:18 UTC -> release.batch_prefetch_v2=false
ben: flag toggle acknowledged. Observing metrics...
(2m) ben: p50 trending down to ~90ms, p95 still elevated but dropping. Throughput recovering slowly. Kernel fallback logs decreasing.
mike: keep an eye for tail-latency tail; kernel fallback can leave warmed nodes in bad states. Recommend also evicting the few pods that had fallback to force fresh kernel selection.
alex: rolling restart on affected hosts now: ``kubectl rollout restart deployment/runtime --selector=slice=thin-slice-eu-west-1``
priya: coordinating with SRE to avoid cascading restarts. Throttling canary to 0% while we stabilize. deploy-bot: scaling canary traffic -> 40% -> 0% (manual override) at 09:25 UTC.
emma: Pinged account exec for acme-payments, telling them we're investigating and already applied mitigation. They'll escalate if they see impact on checkout flow.
ben: logs snippet showing kernel fallback pattern:
```
[09:14:23] kernel_selector.cpp:142 warning: kernel_launch_timeout, selecting fallback kernel-compat-avx
[09:14:23] batch_manager.cpp:87 info: batch queue depth=312 (target 64), kvcache_miss=0.78
[09:14:24] inference.cpp:413 error: slow_dispatch path taken, dispatch_time=1200ms
```
mike: next steps: monitor 15m, if p95 <= 600ms and throughput > 90% baseline -> close incident. If not, prepare rollback to v3.13 (rollout-id rl-2026-10-29-44b).
priya: logging actions and handoff plan. I'm going to escalate to runtime lead @alex for post-mortem and to validate kernel selector revert. If we need rollback, I'll authorize.
alex: I'll take lead for post-mortem and kernel revert. Preliminary hypothesis: combination of `batch_prefetch_v2` + larger default `batch_size_hint` exposes a window where lightweight thin-slice hosts hit a memory jitter causing kernel selector timeouts -> fallback kernels slower and less efficient -> batch head-of-line blocking. Plan: add protective guard rails in kernel selector and add a conservative backoff for prefetching in thin slices.
(15m) ben: metrics look stable after flag-off + restarts. p95 back to ~520ms then down to 480ms, throughput ~95% baseline. No additional customer complaints.
priya: handing off to alex (runtime lead) for ongoing remediation and post-mortem. I'll stay available for followups. Handoff notes: mitigation applied 09:18 UTC (flag off), canary scaled to 0% at 09:25 UTC, rolling restarts 09:20-09:28 UTC, partial customer impact (acme-payments) notified.
alex: acknowledged. Creating incident ticket INC-2026-1189 and will run targeted evals on thin-slice hosts.
emma: I'll send an advisory to account team with timeline and mitigation summary.
incidents-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: Canary traffic removed and mitigations applied. Resolution noted at 09:40 UTC. :white_check_mark:
priya: closing on-call, handing to next oncall (mike) for late-night watch. Mike, please validate the staging canary when you have a window and sign off before re-enabling `release.batch_prefetch_v2`.
mike: will validate and coordinate with alex tomorrow. Adding postmortem owners: alex, ben, priya, emma.
(1h) alex: postmortem draft started — root cause hypothesis and remediation actions in doc: /docs/incidents/INC-2026-1189-postmortem.md. Will include regression test for kernel selector under memory jitter and a gate in release pipeline to require thin-slice smoke tests.
priya: thanks team — good quick mitigation. Closing thread.
